tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification in development builds

The project's current recorded decision is that verification is mandatory on all builds, development environments included, so TLS certificate verification must be enabled in development builds and is not to be disabled there. This is consistent with the recorded requirement that HTTPS be used everywhere with no plaintext exceptions.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md` with a one-paragraph statement of the current decision: verification is mandatory on all builds, development included. So TLS certificate verification stays enabled in development builds. The paragraph also says this fits the recorded rule that HTTPS is required everywhere with no plaintext exceptions.

The recorded decision is a session note (#S1, "verification on all builds should be mandatory, including in development environments"), plus observation #18 on HTTPS everywhere. #S1 doesn't say "TLS certificate" explicitly. I read it as covering TLS because it sits between the HTTPS decisions, so check that reading if it matters.

The earlier plain-HTTP exception (#17) was reversed by #18, so I left it out.

Separately, `gin_test.go` and `gin_integration_test.go` use `InsecureSkipVerify: true` in test code. Nothing recorded covers that, so I left it out of the policy and didn't change the tests.
